channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: Bain puts US holiday sales above $1 trillion, up 4.5%
item.description: McKinsey finds 43% of shoppers planning to spend less on jewelry and 18% planning to spend more. Only 10% name jewelry or accessories as a top category.

item.title: HRD Antwerp opens Mumbai lab grading 2,000 diamonds a day
item.description: The renovated Bandra Kurla Complex laboratory raises capacity 30% and adds 40 full-time staff. India already provides 59% of HRD Antwerp's group revenue and is forecast to grow 15% this year.

item.title: RAPI 1-carat adds 0.59% since 8 August, now published daily
item.description: Rapaport's index page now carries a dated level for every day of a 30-day window. The 0.50-carat leads at 2.38% and the 2-carat is the only faller, down 0.25%.

item.title: Gold sheds $25.10 to $4,403.90 in the Labor Day session
item.description: Silver fell 0.75% to $65.596 and platinum a dollar to $1,815.00. Palladium alone rose, adding $8.00 to $1,377.00 on Kitco's bid at 10:04 UTC.

item.title: HK$20m ruby earrings lead Sotheby's Hong Kong sale on 17 September
item.description: Two pear-shaped Burmese rubies of 5.08 and 5.20 carats top a sale of more than 200 lots. Nine of the ten costliest lots are led by a coloured stone.

item.title: Antwerp's $19.1bn trade turns to India as De Wever visits Mumbai
item.description: Bart De Wever went to Mumbai's diamond bourse, a first for a Belgian prime minister on GJEPC's account. Gem and jewellery trade between the two countries stood at $3.5bn in 2025-26.

item.title: Gareth Penny gives CIBJO an 8-point plan for natural diamonds
item.description: Gareth Penny leads the consortium bidding for De Beers. He told the confederation's centenary congress in Vicenza that the trade is in a real crisis and that De Beers must lead beyond its own business.

item.title: Edge counts August jewelry sales up 5%, units down 8%
item.description: The average retail sale rose 14% against August 2025. Diamond jewelry carried the month, its dollars up 8% on 9% fewer units, while sterling silver and alternative metals lost both.

item.title: $55,000 sapphire necklace leads Bonhams California on 24 September
item.description: Four sapphires of 3.25 to 5.65 carats sit in the top lot of a sale of more than 200 pieces. Tiffany, Hermes and David Webb fill out the estate names.

item.title: Rolex sends 4 one-off Daytonas to Phillips on 28 September
item.description: The set was conceived for a single buyer at about $4.9 million before Rolex switched it to auction. Proceeds are split evenly between the Federer Foundation and Re:wild.

item.title: Chow Tai Seng's Hong Kong arm joins the Shanghai Gold Exchange
item.description: The board filing, numbered 2026-043 and dated 2 September, says the exchange admitted the wholly-owned subsidiary as an international member. First-half revenue at the parent fell 20.79%.

item.title: Perth Mint gold sales fall 22% while the metal gains 10%
item.description: Silver sales dropped 31% on the month and platinum 45%, in figures the mint published on 4 September. Holdings in its gold-backed product rose 3.43% to 395,871 ounces.

item.title: SEC sues Lugano ex-CEO over $1bn of fictitious revenue
item.description: The complaint, filed 31 August in California, covers conduct from 2021 to 2025. A restatement later cut Lugano's net assets at acquisition from $179 million to $5 million.

item.title: Movado first-half operating income rises 409% to $21.9 million
item.description: Net sales for the six months to 31 July reached $312.2 million, up 6.3%, on a gross margin of 58.4% against 54.1%. The figures come from Movado Group's quarterly filing with the SEC.

item.title: 17 weeks in, Watches of Switzerland holds 5-10% guidance
item.description: The group also reiterated 40 to 80 basis points of adjusted EBIT margin expansion for the full year. Capital expenditure is guided at £60 million to £70 million, with free cash flow conversion near 70%.

item.title: Christie's watch sales rise 39% as Guillemin takes global role
item.description: Geneva's May rare watch sale made $42.2 million, which the house calls its highest various-owner watch result. Hong Kong made $35.7 million in the same month, up 40% on the year.

item.title: IBJA gold adds ₹2,549 after a ₹4,651 two-day fall
item.description: The India Bullion and Jewellers Association put 10 grams of 24-carat gold at ₹1.54 lakh on 3 September. Silver rose ₹4,420 to ₹2.33 lakh a kilogram, after falling ₹8,803 across the two days before.

item.title: 1-carat polished up 0.5% in August, first rise in 15 months
item.description: Rapaport's index shows small rounds leading the recovery, with the 0.30-carat up 2% and the 0.50-carat up 2.5%. The 3-carat slipped 0.4% after 18 months without a move.

item.title: $119.30 back on gold: the first higher mark since 28 August
item.description: Gold $4,426.80, silver $65.58, platinum $1,762.00, palladium $1,348.00 at 05:59 ET, every one higher. Gold recovers 40.17% of the $297.00 it lost after 28 August, and stays $177.70 below that mark.

item.title: IIGJ and IIT Madras split 90 hours, and 60 of them are physics
item.description: The Indian Institute of Gems & Jewellery and IIT Madras's InCent-LGD centre launched a 90-hour hybrid certificate on 2 September. Sixty of the ninety hours are IIT Madras's, and only twelve are on campus.

item.title: $297.00 off gold and $170.00 off platinum: every mark lower since Friday
item.description: Gold $4,307.50 and platinum $1,713.00 at press time, the fifth consecutive lower mark for each on this tape. Gold has given up 6.45% since 28 August, platinum 9.03%, and silver more than either at 9.68%.

item.title: $675 for the one-carat while the index rises $12: lab-grown splits in two
item.description: CaratRadar's one-carat average fell $12 to $675, a third straight lower mark from Monday's $700. Its whole-market index rose $12 to $1,535 over the same day, and active listings passed 1.21 million.

item.title: £59,000 in Penzance: a steel Patek beats its low estimate 11.8 times
item.description: A stainless Calatrava reference 448, found during a Cornish house clearance, sold at Hansons on 25 August against a £5,000 to £10,000 estimate. The winning bid came by telephone from Hong Kong.

item.title: Two CEOs and a president: Kering rewires Pomellato, DoDo and its Italian holding
item.description: Charlotte Fournet takes Pomellato and Krizia Cucurachi takes DoDo on 15 September, both reporting to Jean-Marc Duplaix. Sabina Belli, Pomellato's chief since 2015, becomes president of Kering Italia.

item.title: $24,900 for a rubber Big Bang: Hublot prices texture as a material, not a finish
item.description: The Big Bang Original Soft Touch launched on 1 September in All Black and All Red at $24,900, on the in-house HUB1280 column-wheel chronograph built at Nyon.

item.title: 1,600 square feet at South Coast Plaza: Jessica McCormack takes the West Coast
item.description: The London jeweller's second US store opened on 28 August at 3333 Bristol Street, Costa Mesa, in a Jewel Court that already holds Cartier, Chopard, Piaget and Harry Winston. Rodeo Drive follows in 2027.

item.title: $4,366.10 gold and $1,753.00 platinum: the board is back at 19 August
item.description: Gold fell 1.85% at press time, silver 3.13%, platinum 2.12% and palladium 3.84%. Three of the four now sit within 2.1% of their 19 August marks, and August's rally is gone.

item.title: $687 a carat: lab-grown's one-dollar drift becomes a thirteen-dollar step
item.description: CaratRadar's one-carat average fell $13 to $687 on 1 September, down 1.86% in a session. Every other move on this tape since 5 August was three dollars or less.

item.title: RMB 3.641 billion, down 20.79%: Chow Tai Seng's margin rose anyway
item.description: Revenue fell 20.79% and net profit 24.24% in the six months to 30 June. Gross margin rose 6.61 points to 36.95%, and second-quarter profit fell 54.2%.

item.title: $2,666.92 a polished carat, $82.66 a rough one: Antwerp's two books split
item.description: Antwerp exported 1.15% fewer polished carats for 15.99% more dollars in the seven months to July, and 10.90% more rough carats for 17.73% fewer dollars. Per carat, polished rose 17.34% and rough fell 25.82%.
